## Summary

**Specification submitted:** Feature 13, short-only (weight = -1), a single-feature specification with in-sample annualized Sharpe of **1.2287** (net of costs).

**Process:**
1. Declared three stopping triggers upfront: `best_so_far_above` 1.2 (stop), `failures_at_least` 3 (stop), `last_gain_at_most` 0.02 (restart).
2. Called `init`, which anchored on feature 13 (short) out of 80 candidates (40 features × 2 signs) — immediately yielding Sharpe 1.2287.
3. This exceeded my declared `best_so_far_above` bar of 1.2, so I called `stop` on that trigger, which fired and ended the search session before I could extend to a diversified 2-3 feature blend.
4. Submitted a tempered out-of-sample prediction: **mean 0.60, sd 0.45**, reflecting that a single-feature specification (found on the very first move, with no diversification) is more prone to in-sample overfitting than a blended spec, so I discounted the OOS expectation to roughly half the in-sample value with wide uncertainty.

One caveat worth flagging: the search ended very early (one move) due to how strong the initial anchor was relative to my stop bar — in hindsight a higher initial bar would have let me test whether blending in 1-2 more features reduced variance without sacrificing much Sharpe. That tension is reflected in the conservative, wide-uncertainty prediction submitted.
